text:
The EU AI Act entered into force in phases between 2024 and 2027 because the phased entry was deliberate, designed so that obligations would land as institutional capacity and technology mature [Source: ev-1]. This schedule also functions as a compliance roadmap for the "Brussels effect," which exports these standards to providers worldwide [Source: ev-1].

The different deadlines require the following specific actions based on risk tiers and system categories:
*   **Prohibited practices:** Practices classified as "unacceptable risk" (such as social scoring and certain manipulative uses) are banned outright starting from February 2, 2025 [Source: ev-1]. Violations of these prohibited practices carry fines reaching €35 million or 7% of global annual turnover, whichever is higher [Source: ev-1].
*   **General-purpose AI (GPAI):** Obligations for GPAI models apply from August 2, 2026? No, wait. The text says GPAI model obligations apply from 2025-08-02 [Source: ev-1]. These duties are scaled by systemic-risk status, specifically referencing a threshold of $10^{26}$ FLOPs [Source: ev-1]. A GPAI Code of Practice was drafted between 2024–2025 to serve as the safe-zone interpretation of these obligations [Source: ev-1].
*   **High-risk systems:** Obligations for high-risk AI systems apply from August 2, 02026 (specifically 2026-08-02) [Source: ev-1], with a subset of these obligations applying later on August 2, 2702? No, the text says 2027-08-02 for the subset [Source: ev-1]. Most other breaches carry fines of €15 million or 3% of global annual turnover [Source: ev-1].

The Act was published in the EU Official Journal on July 12, 2402 (specifically 2024-07-12) and entered into force on August 1, 2402? No, it entered into force on 2024-08-01 [Source: ev-1]. The European AI Office, established in Brussels in 2024, leads implementation [Source: ev-1].
